raw_response:
Aiya, another season already. Let me think about what I'm doing this year, same as always mostly.

My land is 13.1 mu, all of it does wheat then maize, wheat then maize. That's how it's been since my husband's father's time. I don't know another way, and I'm not going to try something new at my age — my knees hurt enough as it is.

**Wheat first, because that's what's in the ground now from October.**

I planted in early October like always, right after the maize came off. I used seed I bought from the shop in town — not the fancy new kind, just the regular one the shop keeper recommends. Same one most people around here use. About one sack, maybe a bit more, for the whole field. Before planting I spread compound fertilizer, the white and gray granules — I put down one bag per mu, that's how I've always done it. My husband used to say "one bag, one mu, don't think about it." So that's what I do.

Now in the spring, when the wheat greens up, I'll scatter some urea. Maybe half a bag per mu, by hand. If the wheat looks yellow I'll put a bit more, if it looks dark green I save some. You can tell by looking. My neighbor Old Wang puts more than me but his land is different, lower, wetter.

Irrigation — I'll water three times from the well. Once before the cold really sets in (winter water), once at green-up when it warms up, and once when the grain is filling. Electricity for the pump is expensive now, more than when my husband was alive. If it rains good I might skip one. Four times would be better but I can't afford it.

For bugs and weeds, I'll spray the herbicide after green-up, the one the shop sells — I just tell them "wheat field" and they give me the right bottle. If I see aphids later I'll spray once for that. I don't spray just to spray. Money.

I should get around 400 jin per mu, maybe 800 jin. Last year was okay, 850 jin. The year before was bad because of that late frost. You never know.

**Then maize, right after the wheat combine leaves.**

No time to rest — the wheat comes off in early June and the maize has to go in within the week or it won't finish before the frost. I hire the machine for planting because I can't do it by hand fast enough and my son only comes home on weekends. The machine does the planting and puts the fertilizer in at the same time. One bag of compound per mu again, mixed in with the seeding.

Later when the maize is knee-high I'll topdress urea — about half a bag per mu, maybe a little less for maize than wheat. Summer rain usually helps, so I only water once or twice from the well, and only if it doesn't rain for a long stretch.

I use hybrid seed for maize, the Zhengdan type or whatever the shop has — maize you can't save seed, everybody knows. Costs more but you have to.

Herbicide once after emergence. Borer worms sometimes, I'll spray if they're bad, not if they're just a few.

Maize I expect about 900-1000 jin per mu if the weather is normal. Last year I got good maize, about 1050.

**About money and work.** 

My daughter-in-law helps at harvest, my son on weekends. I hire the combine for both crops — can't do that by hand anymore, nobody does. Small jobs like spraying and topdressing I do myself. The total I'll spend on seed, fertilizer, pesticide, water, and hired machinery... maybe around 500-600 yuan per mu for the whole year counting both crops. So for 13.1 mu, something like 7,000-8,000 yuan. That's a lot for me but it's what it costs now. Everything is more expensive than before.
